title: Rings and Rods
statement:
Ten rods are numbered `0` to `9`, and `n` coloured rings have been dropped onto them. The string `rings` lists the rings two characters at a time: in each pair the first character is the ring's colour (`'R'` for red, `'G'` for green, `'B'` for blue) and the second is the digit of the rod it sits on. For example, `"R3G2"` means a red ring on rod 3 and a green ring on rod 2.

Return how many rods carry at least one ring of each of the three colours.
constraints: Every character at an even index of rings is 'R', 'G' or 'B'
Every character at an odd index of rings is a digit from '0' to '9'
notes:
## Intuition

All that matters for a rod is which colours it has seen, not how many rings or in what order. A map from each rod to the set of colours on it collects exactly that in one pass over the pairs. A rod counts when its set has grown to all three colours. The slower alternative checks each of the ten rods against each colour by rescanning the string.

## Approach

1. Create an empty map `colorsOnRod` from rod digit to a set of colours.
2. Walk the string two characters at a time: `color` is `rings[i]` and `rod` is `rings[i + 1]`.
3. Give the rod an empty set the first time it appears, then add `color` to it. A set ignores repeated colours.
4. Count the rods whose set has size `3` and return that `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`rings = "B0B6G0R6R0R6G9"` gives the pairs `B0`, `B6`, `G0`, `R6`, `R0`, `R6`, `G9`. After the scan, rod `0` has `{B, G, R}`, rod `6` has `{B, R}` (the second red adds nothing) and rod `9` has `{G}`. Only rod `0` has three colours, so the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one constant-time step per ring, plus at most ten rods to count.
- Space: O(1): at most ten sets of at most three colours.

## Pitfalls

- Counting rings instead of distinct colours is wrong: `"R5R5R5"` has three rings but one colour.
- Step through the string by `2`; stepping by `1` mixes colours and rod digits.
- A rod is counted once, however many full sets of rings it holds.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `colorsOnRod` | map from rod digit to the set of colours seen on it |
| `i` | index of the current pair's colour character |
| `color`, `rod` | the current ring's colour and rod |
| `count` | rods found with all three colours |

narration.13: Look at the colour set of each rod that holds at least one ring.
narration.14: A set of size 3 means red, green and blue are all present.
narration.18: Return the number of rods with all three colours.
